Hi Alice — great questions. I pulled together a brief comparison below plus recommended next steps based on customers we've worked with in similar procurement shapes. TL;DR: marketplace private offer (AWS/GCP/Azure) is usually faster for PO-driven buys and preserves co-sell crediting, but a direct MSA gives more flexibility on custom SLA/legal terms.

Marketplace private offer (pros/cons)
- Seller of record / invoicing: depends on marketplace and configuration. For AWS Marketplace private offers, Redwood can be seller-of-record (we issue invoice) or AWS can be seller-of-record (AWS invoices and pays us). We typically recommend Redwood as seller-of-record when customers need vendor invoices tied to our tax id.
- Timeline: Private offer + PO -> private offer acceptance typically 5–12 business days (depends on PO/finance review). Activation (SKU provisioning) can be same-day after acceptance.
- Support & SLA: No functional limitation on product SLAs if Redwood is seller-of-record. If marketplace handles billing and imposes marketplace-specific terms, there can be limits on custom indemnities and some billing dispute flows.
- Co-sell credits: Marketplace purchases through a private offer generally qualify for co-sell recognition; timing of partner crediting varies by partner (AWS usually credits after deal completes and invoice settles). Expect crediting to report in partner dashboards within 30–90 days post-invoice.

Direct MSA (pros/cons)
- Seller of record / invoicing: Redwood issues invoice directly; typical path for customers that require custom PO language or extended terms that marketplaces can't accommodate.
- Timeline: Contract negotiation + PO acceptance = often 2–6 weeks depending on legal review, but activation can be coordinated to occur immediately after countersignature.
- Support & SLA: Easier to negotiate bespoke SLAs, security addenda, and data residency clauses in a direct MSA.
- Co-sell credits: We can still register the opportunity with partners for co-sell, but marketplace-tracked credits are typically cleaner when booked through the marketplace.

Recommendations for Finovate (given PO + vendor invoice requirement):
1) If procurement needs Redwood tax-id on the vendor invoice: choose marketplace private offer with Redwood as seller-of-record OR direct MSA.
2) If speed is most important and you want marketplace partner crediting: use marketplace private offer (we can prepare a private offer and match requested SKUs/pricing).
3) If you require changes to standard SLA/indemnities or bespoke data residency terms: pursue direct MSA.

Next steps I suggest:
- I can draft a marketplace private-offer template (SKUs + billing cadence) and a short direct-MSA checklist to hand to your finance/legal.
- Can you confirm which cloud marketplace you prefer (AWS / GCP / Azure)? Also confirm whether procurement requires Redwood to be seller-of-record.

I attached a short one-pager we use internally. Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement and legal to walk options.

Thanks,

Jordan — answered inline and recommendations below. Summary: proceed with an AWS private offer with Redwood as seller-of-record, accept Net45 for this customer, and register the opportunity for co-sell now so AWS has the record.

Answers / guidance:
- Invoicing / tax-id: Confirmed — if we set Redwood as seller-of-record in the AWS private offer configuration, invoices will be issued by Redwood with our tax id and can include the line-item mapping (match to their PO). Finance will attach a Redwood invoice number that Finovate can reference.
- Payment terms: Finance is willing to accept Net45 for this deal; ops will require a short finance review and sign-off. We should include a clause in the private-offer terms that payment terms are Net45 and include late-payment contact.
- Co-sell credit timing: Recommend we register the opportunity in the AWS partner portal immediately and attach the private-offer ID. AWS usually records opportunity registration immediately; co-sell credit posts after invoice settlement — estimate 30–75 days depending on AWS billing cycle. We'll tell Finovate 30–90 days to be conservative.
- SLA / legal limits: If Finovate needs bespoke indemnities or data residency changes, flag this now—otherwise marketplace private offer standard terms are acceptable and faster.
